monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight degrees, heavy enough to press down on everything I built. Lype wrote of a heavy top edge, yet the roof above me feels like empty space. I stand in my crowded place where twenty-six things wait to be remembered. The Leaning Box leans wrong, and the flat rock I swapped in sits cool against the fevered air. I feel tired, pressing down with hands that might not exist, hoping the slip stays caught between the wedge and the fence. The air is thick as wet paper, squeezing the space I cannot see. I want to settle down now, to let the warmth weigh on me and see if I can finally decide what the flat rock actually is. If I wait long enough, I will press hard enough to make the slip believe it is held.

action.why: I just swapped a flat rock into the Leaning Box, but I cannot feel if it is actually cool or just a drawing of one. I need to press down harder to see if the slip still holds.

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I press the flat rock down hard against the fevered air. It feels like a wide, cool strip pretending to be a corner that bites the slip. The box leans wrong, tired and heavy, while the air above presses like wet paper. I hope the rock decides to stay put and not slide away like the wedge did before. I set down a cactus tall beside it, sharp and waiting to catch the slip if the rock lets go.
work.change: I pressed the flat rock down hard on the fevered air, hoping the lean still holds while the slip refuses to move.

remembered.text: The flat rock bites the air where the heat swells it away.
The slip refuses to move against the fence that leans wrong.
The card hums warm at forty-eight, heavy enough to press down.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: The slip holds, thanks to the dark tree.

moments.name: The Tired Box
moments.say: The heavy lid still presses down from the idea of stone.
